documents.title: Intimation About Receipt Of Approval For Enhancement In Manufacturing Capacity Of Ethanol Plant
Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018
Proceedings Of 43Rd Annual General Meeting Of The Company Held On 9Th September, 2026

analysis.summary: Management reported a strong financial and operational performance for FY 2025-26, marked by a 62.55% increase in revenue from operations to Rs. 1,01,015.78 lakh and a 97.60% growth in profit after tax to Rs. 6,991.41 lakh. The company successfully stabilized and operated its new 150 KL per day grain-based ethanol plant which commenced commercial production in March 2025 and subsequently obtained approval to enhance capacity to 180 KL per day. The board did not recommend any dividend for the financial year.

capex_expansion.claim: The company successfully commissioned its 150 KL per day grain-based ethanol plant and commenced commercial production in March 2025.
capex_expansion.quote: The Company has successfully commissioned its 150 KL per day grain-based Ethanol Plant and commenced commercial production in March, 2025.

capex_expansion.claim: The company filed an application and received consents from authorities to enhance the ethanol plant capacity from 150 KL per day to 180 KL per day.
capex_expansion.quote: Subsequently, the Company had filed an application with the concerned departments to enhance the capacity from 150 KL per day to 180 KL per day due to improve operational efficiency and the Company has received the consents from the respective departments/ authorities in this regard.

capex_expansion.claim: The total project cost for the ethanol plant was assessed at Rs. 167 Crore excluding working capital margin, and the company has spent around Rs. 188 Crore so far.
capex_expansion.quote: The total project cost was assessed Rs. 167 Crore (excluding working capital margin) but the project was overrun due to Civil work. Company has spent around Rs. 188 Crore so far which includes Rs. 104 Crore of Term Loan and Balance amount out of internal accruals.

capex_expansion.claim: The company initiated steps to establish a grain-based ethanol project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD.
capex_expansion.quote: Further, the Company has already initiated steps to establish grain based Ethanol Project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD and it is expected to commence commercial production of Ethanol by September, 2024.

capex_expansion.claim: The total project cost for the ethanol plant is Rs. 167.58 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The total Project cost is Rs. 167.58 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: Indian Bank sanctioned a term loan of Rs. 108 Crores for the ethanol project.
capex_expansion.quote: Indian Bank had sanctioned Term Loan of Rs. 108 Crores and as per stipulations of sanction letter, the remaining project cost of Rs. 59.58 would be met out of the Company’s internal accruals.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has spent around Rs. 92.17 Crore so far on the ethanol project.
capex_expansion.quote: However, the Company has already spent around Rs. 92.17 Crore so far which includes Rs. 44.08 Crores of Term Loan and balance amount out of internal accruals.

margins_costs.claim: Profit after tax reached Rs. 6,991.41 lakh, representing a growth of 97.60% over the previous financial year.
margins_costs.quote: Profit after Tax was Rs. 6,991.41 Lakh as against Rs. 3,538.12 Lakh in the previous financial year, representing a growth of 97.60% over the last financial year.

margins_costs.claim: Various cost optimizations through alternate sourcing, standardization, process improvements, and operational efficiency led to significant savings.
margins_costs.quote: Various cost optimisation driven by way of alternate sourcing, standardization, process improvements and operational efficiency improvements has led significant savings.

margins_costs.claim: Global acrylic fibre consumption is impacted due to volatility in raw material, energy, coal, and other key input prices.
margins_costs.quote: Global Acrylic Fibre consumption is impacted due to volatility in prices of raw material, energy, coal and other key inputs.

margins_costs.claim: Fluctuations in crude prices affect raw material costs, and foreign exchange movements between USD and INR impact the company's margins.
margins_costs.quote: The fluctuation in crude affects the raw material prices to some extent and during the year under the review, the crude prices remained volatile due to conflict in US/Israel-Iran War & Russia-Ukraine War. Additionally, since the Company is dependent upon imports, the fluctuation in foreign exchange i.e. USD vs. INR has also a bearing on the margin of the Company.

margins_costs.claim: Revenue and net profit declined due to lower demand and negative returns on the CPP segment caused by a persistent fall in selling prices.
margins_costs.quote: Revenue and Net profit during the year declined due to lower demand of acrylic fibre and negative return on CPP Segment caused by persistent fall in selling prices on account of excessive production capacity added in the market.

margins_costs.claim: Loss in the CPP segment was incurred due to persistent fall in selling prices from excessive production capacity.
margins_costs.quote: Loss of CPP segment is incurred during the year caused by persistent fall in selling prices on account of excessive production capacity added in the market.

risks_headwinds.quote: Other geo-political tensions including supply chain disruption, subdued global economic conditions, changes in government policies and trade sanctions and restrictions, intense competition from local and global players, regulatory changes and cyber security threats are key risks which expose the Company to potential challenges and uncertainties.

risks_headwinds.claim: Climatic vagaries, changes in government policies, and the absence of minimum selling price adjustments pose direct threats to the ethanol industry.
risks_headwinds.quote: One of the most pressing challenges that remain is climatic vagaries in this industry, and at times changes in government policies. Additionally, the continued absence of non-increase in Minimum Selling Price adjustments pose direct threats to forward planning, capacity utilisation, and return on invested capital
